chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who is crippled in the right hand or crippled in the left hand who steals, he said: His right hand is cut off in all cases.

key_terms.أَشَلِّ: Crippled or disabled in a limb
key_terms.عَلَى كُلِّ حَالٍ: In all cases / regardless of the situation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on cutting the hand of a thief who is disabled in one hand?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the standard hadd penalty of cutting the right hand applies even if the thief is disabled in one hand, emphasizing the consistency of the ruling regardless of physical impairment. Shia jurists utilize this to discuss whether the cut is always the right hand or adjusted based on the disability, reflecting the principle of applying the literal text unless specific evidence suggests otherwise. It underscores the universality of the hadd in classical fiqh while allowing for scholarly nuance in execution.
